subject: Request: Transitional bill-credit for runtime blocker delaying BrightBridge launch
messages:
From: Sam Ellis <sam@brightbridge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production hold: runtime prefetch/quant issue blocking BrightBridge launch

Mina / team,

Quick heads up — our engineering team hit a runtime regression after the quant rollout last night. Latency spikes on our primary path (embedding+rerank) mean our users see timeouts in peak traffic. We’re in a hard stop for the BrightBridge launch scheduled next week unless we get a workaround.

We’ve pulled logs and attached a short incident summary. This is blocking their go-live and procurement is asking whether Redwood will provide commercial relief if the timeline slips. They were counting on the June contract start and marketing cadence.

Can someone confirm expected mitigation ETA and whether there is precedent for a transitional credit while we patch? They’ve already paused marketing and are asking for written assurance.

—Sam
Sam Ellis
VP Product, BrightBridge
Sam.ellis@brightbridge.ai

Attachments: incident_summary.csv (csv), stack_snapshot.txt (text)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ellis <sam@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production hold: runtime prefetch/quant issue blocking BrightBridge launch

Sam — thanks for the flag and the incident summary. We see the same traces and I’m escalating internally to product and commercial. I’m copying Monica (CS lead) and Karthik (AE) to coordinate the customer-facing plan.

Short answer: we will provide a written commitment on the remediation timeline by EOD PST and a commercial proposal for a bridge credit if remediation takes longer than 72 hours. I’ll follow up with specifics in this thread.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

CC: Monica Patel, Karthik Iyer
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2025 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production hold: runtime prefetch/quant issue blocking BrightBridge launch

Mina / Karthik — I ran a post-mortem with the SEs. Key points:
- Root cause: kernel path mismatch when quantized weights hit long-sequence batch; leads to KV cache thrash and token-level stalls.
- Short-term mitigations: pin to pre-quant model variant or restrict batch size; we can toggle routing for BrightBridge within 1 hour but throughput will drop ~20%.
- Estimated fix (product): 3 business days for a targeted kernel fallback with monitoring; 1–2 days for safe rollback to pre-quant variant.

Customer impact: BrightBridge cannot accept the throughput degradation for initial launch. They want either a rollback or a commercial accommodation for the delay window.

I recommend we offer a timeboxed rebate for the launch period while we deliver the kernel fallback, with a clause: rebate contingent on BrightBridge taking the rollback route if they accept reduced throughput.

Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2025 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production hold: runtime prefetch/quant issue blocking BrightBridge launch

Team — proposal from commercial perspective:
- Offer a transitional bill-credit equal to 25% of expected July invoice (pro-rated) if remediation > 72 hours and customer does not accept rollback.
- If BrightBridge agrees to a controlled rollback to pre-quant variant, offer a reduced credit (12.5%) plus prioritized engineering support and waived onboarding professional services fee.
- Require a signed amendment (DocuSign) capturing the timeline and rollback opt-in.

We need finance sign-off on the threshold and the authority to approve up to $XXK in credits without exec offline. Laura — can you confirm authority and whether this structure is acceptable?

-Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production hold: runtime prefetch/quant issue blocking BrightBridge launch

Quick update from product/eng:
- Rollback to the pre-quant variant is ready as a supported mitigation and can be applied to BrightBridge routing within 90 minutes. We have validated functional fidelity; throughput loss is ~18% but stable.
- Kernel fallback (full fix) is slated for release in 3 business days. We’ll provide a staged canary and monitoring dashboard for BrightBridge.

Recommendation: offer the customer the rollback option (1) with a reduced commercial accommodation (12.5% pro-rated credit for the launch week) and (2) if they opt to wait for the kernel fix, offer a larger transitional credit (20% pro-rated) that expires if fix delivered within 72 hours.

If finance is comfortable with the 20% cap (Laura) I’ll prepare the technical note and the canary plan so CS/SE can present to Sam.

Aditya Rao
VP Product — Redwood Inference
